title: Automated Fault Detection Coverage by Tier of Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# Automated Fault Detection Coverage by Tier

Analytics group table of the fault detection figures fixed for each tier of Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions.

| Tier | Automated fault detection runs | Fault detection rules enabled against the site | Lowest fault priority reported to the owner | Reportable fault notified within (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Utility Bill Tracking Subscription | no | 0 | critical | 10 |
| Metering & Dashboard Subscription | no | 0 | high | 7 |
| Energy Analytics Subscription | no | 0 | medium | 5 |
| Fault Detection & Diagnostics Subscription | yes | 120 | low | 3 |
| Measurement & Verification Program | yes | 180 | low | 3 |
| Managed Energy Performance Program | yes | 260 | informational | 2 |


## Reading the table

- Detection runs only at the Fault Detection & Diagnostics Subscription, the Measurement & Verification Program and the Managed Energy Performance Program. The three lower tiers have 0 rules enabled, and the priority threshold and notification period shown for them describe no live detection.
- The priority scale, from lowest to highest, is informational, low, medium, high, critical. The threshold is the lowest priority that is reported to the owner: a Managed Energy Performance Program reports every priority down to informational; a Fault Detection & Diagnostics Subscription reports low and above.
- The notification period is counted in business days.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Measurement & Verification Program runs 180 rules; a condition flagged at medium priority reaches its low threshold and is notified within 3 business days, while a condition flagged at informational priority falls below the threshold.
